articles.title: Renaissance Architecture
articles.scenario_summary: Added source-safe board-style recognition scenario bounded to selected local source-map anchors.
unsupported_or_removed_claims: Avoid unsupported exact dome-span or capacity claims unless a future local capture gives the exact value.
Treat proportional ratios as exam recognition anchors, not as proof that all Renaissance buildings used one fixed ratio system.
articles.source_locator: UNESCO Florence/Vicenza captures plus HOA Module 2 P2 and Fletcher locators for Brunelleschi, Alberti, Bramante, Palladio, proportional theory, villas, and St. Peter sequence.

articles.title: Baroque Architecture
articles.scenario_summary: Added source-safe board-style recognition scenario bounded to selected local source-map anchors.
unsupported_or_removed_claims: Do not treat every dramatic 17th-century building as Counter-Reformation church space; Versailles is a political-court example.
Do not cite unsupported exact dates for minor churches unless carried by the question source map.
articles.source_locator: UNESCO Versailles and Vatican News Bernini Baldacchino captures plus HOA Module 2 P2 and Fletcher locators for Baroque movement, Bernini, Borromini, Jesuit spatial focus, Versailles, and Rococo transition.

articles.title: Neoclassicism
articles.scenario_summary: Added source-safe board-style recognition scenario bounded to selected local source-map anchors.
unsupported_or_removed_claims: Do not overstate democracy as a universal motive for every Neoclassical building; use it where the question is civic or American.
Treat publication and excavation references as movement catalysts, not as the only causes of Neoclassicism.
articles.source_locator: AOC U.S. Capitol, Monticello, Berlin Brandenburg Gate, Paris Pantheon, HOA Module 2 P3, and Fletcher locators for Enlightenment classicism, Greek Revival, civic symbolism, Monticello, and measured antiquity.

articles.title: Islamic architecture
articles.scenario_summary: Added source-safe board-style recognition scenario bounded to selected local source-map anchors.
unsupported_or_removed_claims: Avoid sweeping claims that Islamic architecture bans all imagery in every context; keep exam answers focused on mosque-safe surface vocabulary.
Treat reused classical columns as a common historical practice, not as a universal rule for every Islamic building.
articles.source_locator: UNESCO Damascus/Cordoba/Jerusalem captures plus HOA Module 3 and Fletcher locators for mosque vocabulary, mihrab, sahn, minaret, iwan, muqarnas, arabesque, calligraphy, and reused columns.

articles.title: Umayyad and Abbasid Architecture
articles.scenario_summary: Added source-safe board-style recognition scenario bounded to selected local source-map anchors.
unsupported_or_removed_claims: Use exact dates only where carried by the local source map or by the question itself; otherwise use century-level statements.
Do not state that Abbasid builders exclusively used brick or that Umayyad builders exclusively used stone.
articles.source_locator: UNESCO Damascus/Samarra/Jerusalem captures plus HOA Module 3 and Fletcher locators for Dome of the Rock, Great Mosque of Damascus, Umayyad reuse/adaptation, Abbasid Baghdad/Samarra, brick, stucco, palaces, and spiral minaret.
